title: Store a colour in a name
summary: Less variables start with @. A variable lets you reuse a value such as a colour or a spacing size.

blocks.text: Less variables start with @. A variable lets you reuse a value such as a colour or a spacing size.
Use Less 4 on your computer. Install Node.js first. Save examples as lesson.less, then run npx lessc lesson.less lesson.css. The browser loads lesson.css; this site does not build Less.

blocks.title: Store a colour in a name

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: Each `color: @ink` uses that value when Less writes the CSS output.

blocks.text: Both rules have navy as their text colour after compilation.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: The @ in a variable is not part of the CSS property name. Write color: @ink, not @color: ink.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Change ink to teal and build the file again.
